# Complete Algorithm Index

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_catalog_docs.py; edit catalog.yaml. -->

The original syllabus contains **256 entries** in **35 categories**, mapped to **235 unique canonical topics**. Every original label is retained below in its original category and order. Repeated topics link to one canonical folder; meaningful variants have their own records.

Status describes catalog progress. A planning README is an outline of future scope and does not mean the full algorithm article, Python or C++ implementation, or algorithm tests exist.

Foundation checks validate repository structure; they are separate from tests of completed algorithms.

## Canonicalization decisions

- BFS, DFS, A* Search, the repeated graph algorithms, CNNs, Minimax, genetic algorithms, simulated annealing, PSO, and ACO share canonical topics across their original memberships.
- Exhaustive Search and Brute Force Search retain both syllabus labels and share one finite-candidate enumeration topic.
- Vanilla Autoencoders and Autoencoders for Dimensionality Reduction share a reconstruction autoencoder with a bottleneck representation. Denoising, sparse, and variational autoencoders remain distinct variants.
- LDA classification and supervised LDA projection have separate canonical folders because their prediction and transformation contracts are meaningful variants. Their shared mathematics is linked explicitly.
- HMM part-of-speech tagging, tree level-order traversal, recursive versus bitmask subset generation, backtracking versus dynamic-programming subset sum, and the two maximum-subarray formulations remain meaningful variants with separate contracts.
- Dynamic Policy Optimization remains blocked until the maintainer identifies the intended source. Direct Preference Optimization is not substituted. See [terminology decisions](terminology-decisions.md).

The machine-readable source is [catalog.yaml](../catalog.yaml); full documentation and implementation standards are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).
